env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection. Disclose unknown reply timing and do not infer reply links from speaker order alone.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Computation and source suitability:
  - Use code for raw counts, regex/literal matching, supplied numeric columns and fixed
    computational recipes. Use a prompt when the measurement requires understanding meaning.
    Do not add semantic filtering to a raw count or URL detector merely because outcome text
    may occur in its source. Disclose that contamination risk; raw text is not outcome-free.
  - Semantic feature specs must exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome
    resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence of the construct. Generic
    platform/delta-rule discussion remains eligible. Explicitly requested semantic exclusions
    remain part of any measurement; never remove one just to force code.
  - Use current supplied text unless the hypothesis restricts time. Deleting edits does not
    recover initial/pre-outcome text. No supplied comment/edit timestamps establish timing.
    If a required temporal measurement is unavailable, explain it and set term=null.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring a different outcome or an
    outcome-revealing predictor is unsupported: preserve the claim, explain it and set
    term=null rather than substituting another test or a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: arg_compares_to_science_history_norms
features.definition: Does the original argument explicitly compare its subject to an established scientific or historical norm?
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's argument body; ignore title). Return 1 if the OP's own text makes an explicit comparison between the topic/claim and an established scientific norm/standard/consensus or an established historical norm/precedent (e.g., 'just as in the scientific consensus on X', 'unlike historical norm of Y'). Return 0 if no such explicit comparison exists. Do not count mere mentions without comparison, quotations attributed to others unless the OP adopts them as the comparison, or any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting the outcome, or post-outcome resolution updates. Missing or empty argument gives null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose argument has arg_compares_to_science_history_norms=1 have the same view-change (delta) rate as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions whose argument has arg_compares_to_science_history_norms=1 have lower view-change (delta) than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Presence interpreted as binary. Uses current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded from semantic judgment but timing not recoverable). Association only; OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: arg_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection
features.definition: Does the OP's argument explicitly express fear of social rejection or isolation?
features.spec: Read only the argument text. Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly express fear, worry or dread of being socially rejected, ostracized, excluded, judged by others into losing belonging, or isolated/alone because of their view or its expression. Return 0 otherwise (including when only implied). Do not count quoted text from others unless the OP adopts it as their own feeling. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits and reports of the outcome as evidence. Return null if argument is missing or empty/malformed.

features.name: arg_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense
features.definition: Does the OP's argument state beliefs without any emotional self-defense?
features.spec: Read only the argument text. Return 1 if the OP states beliefs or reasons and contains no emotional self-defense (e.g., no pre-emptive protecting of feelings or self-image, no appeals to being hurt, attacked, judged or rejected, no defensive justification of oneself against anticipated social reactions). Return 0 if any such emotional self-defense is present. Attribute only the OP's own assertions, not unadopted quotations. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits and reports of the outcome as evidence. Return null if argument is missing or empty/malformed.

decomposed.h0: Rows with arg_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection and rows with arg_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense have the same view-change rate.
decomposed.h1: Rows with arg_expresses_fear_of_social_rejection have a lower view-change rate than rows with arg_states_beliefs_without_emotional_self_defense.
decomposed.note: The claim compares fear group (A) with a named no-self-defense group (B). In the A+B model each coefficient is relative to the neither group, so beta_A is not beta_A - beta_B, and no single coefficient expresses the requested contrast; term=null. Overlap and neither cases are preserved (neither = other self-defense without social fear, etc.). Argument text is current text and may contain edits/outcome announcements; no pre-outcome snapshot is available. Measurements are semantic LLM judgments of linguistic expression, not measured traits. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment cite a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a named real policy, law, organization or jurisdiction that actually operates or operated) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment itself cites a specific, concrete institutional precedent (e.g., a named law, policy, court, agency, organization, or country/state/city program) presented as actually in operation or having operated, as support for its counter-argument. Return 0 if no comment does (including purely hypothetical institutions, vague references, or only abstract principles). A precedent mentioned only in a quotation of someone else counts only if the commenter adopts it as support. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements or reports of the outcome. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

features.name: any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment rely on abstract normative principles (general moral or ethical principles, rights or values) as its basis?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment's counter-argument rests on abstract normative principles (e.g., general appeals to fairness, justice, rights, liberty, duty, what ought to be) stated in general terms rather than anchored in a specific real institutional precedent. Return 0 if no comment does. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements or reports of the outcome. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: There is no difference in the probability of view change between discussions whose counter-arguments cite functioning institutional precedents and those relying on abstract normative principles.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with counter-arguments citing specific functioning institutional precedents (any_comment_cites_functioning_institutional_precedent) have a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles (any_comment_relies_on_abstract_normative_principles).
decomposed.note: The claim is a comparison of precedent-citing vs abstract-principle comments. The two binary features overlap and can both be 0 or both be 1. With the additive formula, no single coefficient equals beta_precedent minus beta_abstract, so term=null; no difference score was invented. Operational assumptions: presence (any comment) is used as no quantity was specified; the comparison is at discussion level. Source risk: OC_comments may contain outcome announcements; the prompts exclude them. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: What is the supplied log-transformed length value for the discussion?
features.spec: df['supplied_log_length'] = pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce'). Use the supplied value as-is (no recomputation, no log-base assumption); missing or non-numeric gives null.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.note: Uses the supplied log_length column as given; its construction, source text, log base and timing relative to the outcome are undocumented, and it is not equated with argument word count. It may include post-outcome text. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; the result is an association, not a causal effect.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: argument_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: Does the OP's argument contain at least one explicit admission of the OP's own uncertainty (e.g., not sure, might be wrong, could be mistaken)?
features.spec: Read only `argument`. Output 1 if the OP's own text explicitly admits their own uncertainty, doubt or fallibility about their view or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'I'm unsure'); else 0. Count only the OP's own assertions, not quoted or attributed text from others unless the OP adopts it. Generic hedging words without an explicit admission do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty argument gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

features.name: argument_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: Does the OP's argument explicitly assert absolute certainty about their view (e.g., 'there is no doubt', 'absolutely certain', 'impossible to be wrong')?
features.spec: Read only `argument`. Output 1 if the OP's own text explicitly asserts absolute certainty or that their view cannot be wrong (e.g., 'I am 100% sure', 'there is no doubt', 'undeniably'); else 0. Count only the OP's own assertions, not quoted or attributed text from others unless the OP adopts it. Ordinary confident claims without explicit absolute-certainty language do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty argument gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose original argument admits uncertainty (`argument_admits_uncertainty`) have the same probability of view change as those asserting absolute certainty (`argument_asserts_absolute_certainty`).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with `argument_admits_uncertainty` have a higher probability of view change than those with `argument_asserts_absolute_certainty`.
decomposed.note: The claim compares uncertainty-admitting arguments with absolute-certainty arguments. In the chosen formula each coefficient is relative to the omitted baseline (neither), so neither coefficient equals beta_A - beta_B; no single coefficient expresses the requested contrast, hence term=null. Overlap and neither cases exist and are preserved. Both features read current argument text, which may contain edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); semantic prompts exclude those announcements. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count
features.definition: How many distinct factual premises stated in the OP's argument are challenged by the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Read the OP's argument text. Identify the distinct factual (empirical, checkable, non-evaluative) premises asserted by the OP in the argument. Count how many of these distinct premises are directly challenged (disputed, contradicted, or shown to be false/unsupported) by at least one comment in OC_comments. Each premise counts once regardless of how many comments challenge it; one comment challenging several distinct premises counts each. Do not count challenges to values, opinions, or logic that do not dispute a factual claim. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome in argument or comments as evidence. Comments quoting OP are only challenges if the comment itself disputes the premise. Output a non-negative integer. If OC_comments is a valid empty list, or argument contains no factual premises, output 0; if argument or OC_comments is missing or malformed, output null.

decomposed.h0: distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count has no association with view change (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher distinct_factual_premises_challenged_count is associated with a higher probability of view change (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises" is measured as the count of distinct OP factual premises challenged by at least one comment; no threshold of "multiple" is imposed (a linear count term). Comment list order and timing are unknown. Argument text and comments may contain outcome announcements/edits; the prompt excludes them as evidence, but the current text is not a pre-outcome snapshot. Fact vs. value premise classification is judged by the annotator. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: oc_comment_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments by other users are in the discussion's comment list?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; return len(list). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed JSON gives null. Counts comments, not distinct commenters.

decomposed.h0: oc_comment_count has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher oc_comment_count is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (fewer comments, lower likelihood).
decomposed.note: "Fewer counter-argument responses" is operationalized as a lower count of comments in OC_comments (available comments by other users), tested linearly with OLS (linear probability). The list may be a sampled or truncated subset of all responses, and it may include comments made after or because of a view change; its timing is unknown. This is an association, not a causal effect.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: How many distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view are made across the posted comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Count the number of distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view across all comments: separate reasons/points challenging the OP's position; the same argument repeated in several comments or within one comment counts once; one comment can contribute several distinct counter-arguments. Do not count agreement, questions without an argument, jokes, or pure clarification. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output a non-negative integer; empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

features.name: has_three_plus_counterarguments
features.definition: Are there at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments?
features.spec: df['has_three_plus_counterarguments'] = (df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3).astype(int), null where `distinct_counterargument_count` is null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments (has_three_plus_counterarguments=1) have the same likelihood of OP view change as those with fewer.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_plus_counterarguments=1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with fewer than three.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "distinct" means non-duplicated argumentative points, counted across available comments only (list is not necessarily complete or chronological). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Comments may include outcome announcements; the prompt excludes them as evidence. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_has_absolute_certainty_marker
features.definition: Does the original post title use absolute certainty markers (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'definitely', 'undeniably', 'everyone', 'no one', 'obviously')?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title itself uses at least one marker expressing absolute certainty or universality about the claim (e.g., always, never, definitely, certainly, undeniably, obviously, absolutely, without doubt, all/every/no one/nobody, 100%). Return 0 if none is present, including hedged or merely opinionated titles ('I think', 'should'). Judge the title author's own assertion; markers inside quoted text attributed to others do not count unless adopted. Ignore any view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Return null if the title is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between title_has_absolute_certainty_marker and the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Titles with title_has_absolute_certainty_marker=1 are associated with a lower likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Presence of any absolute certainty marker is assumed (no count/intensity specified). The marker list is illustrative; the judgment is semantic. Titles are the OP's current text and could in principle contain edited content, though titles rarely include outcome announcements. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: Does the original post (title or argument) explicitly invite critique or use tentative language when stating its view?
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions either explicitly invite critique/challenge/counterarguments (e.g. 'change my view', 'tell me why I'm wrong', 'I'm open to being convinced') or express the OP's view with tentative/hedged language (e.g. 'I think', 'maybe', 'might', 'it seems', 'I'm not sure'). Return 0 if neither appears. Count only the OP's own wording, not quotations of others unless adopted. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits and reports of the outcome. Return null if both title and argument are missing or empty.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarations
features.definition: Does the original post (title or argument) state its view using absolute, definitive declarations?
features.spec: Read title and argument (the OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP states its own view with absolute/definitive declarations (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'there is no doubt', flat categorical claims without hedging). Return 0 otherwise. Count only the OP's own assertions, not unadopted quotations. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits and reports of the outcome. Return null if both title and argument are missing or empty.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose OP invites critique or uses tentative language (`op_invites_critique_or_tentative`) have the same view-change rate as those whose OP uses absolute declarations (`op_uses_absolute_declarations`).
decomposed.h1: View-change rates are higher for OPs with `op_invites_critique_or_tentative` than for OPs with `op_uses_absolute_declarations`.
decomposed.note: The claim compares two named groups, so the required contrast is beta_invite minus beta_absolute, which is not a single coefficient in this formula. I did not build a difference score, so term is null. Both measurements are kept; overlap and neither cases are possible. Measures use current OP text (title and argument), which may include edits or outcome announcements and is not guaranteed pre-outcome. The prompt specs exclude outcome announcements. Hedging and absolutism are judged by an LLM with no fixed scale.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly cite a specific real-world example as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by users other than the OP. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific real-world example (a named or concretely identifiable actual person, event, case, place, organization, study, or documented real situation, including the commenter's own concrete real experience) as support for its argument. Return 0 if no comment does (only abstract reasoning, generalities, or hypotheticals). Hypothetical or invented scenarios do not count. Do not count OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates, or reports of the outcome as examples. Valid empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example has no association with the likelihood of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows where any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example is 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than rows where it is 0.
decomposed.note: Unspecified quantity treated as presence in at least one comment. OLS on binary delta (linear probability model); association only. Comments may contain outcome-related text; the semantic spec excludes it. Comment order/timing unknown, so examples may follow or not precede the view change. Operational assumption: own concrete real experiences count as real-world examples.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: any_measured_logical_reasoning_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counterargument comment present measured, logical reasoning (calm, reasoned argumentation with explicit logical steps or evidence)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment, by its own assertions, presents measured and logical reasoning: a calm tone with explicit reasoning steps, premises-to-conclusion argument or evidence-based inference. Return 0 if none qualifies. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Overlap with aggression in other or the same comments is allowed; judge this feature independently.

features.name: any_emotionally_aggressive_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counterargument comment contain emotional aggression (hostile, angry, insulting or contemptuous language toward the OP or their view)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment, by its own assertions, contains emotional aggression: hostile, angry, insulting, contemptuous or belittling language directed at the OP or their view. Return 0 if none does. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed OC_comments gives null. Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Judge independently of the logical reasoning feature; a comment may qualify for both.

decomposed.h0: Holding `any_emotionally_aggressive_comment` fixed, `any_measured_logical_reasoning_comment` has no association with delta, i.e. the logical-reasoning effect is no greater than the aggression effect.
decomposed.h1: Rows with a measured logical reasoning comment are more associated with OP view change than rows with an emotionally aggressive comment.
decomposed.note: The claim is a comparison (logical reasoning vs emotional aggression), requiring beta_logical - beta_aggressive. In the OLS formula the two coefficients are separate and no single term expresses that contrast, so term=null; no difference score is invented. Overlap (both present) and neither cases exist. Presence (any comment) is assumed since no quantity was specified. Comments are unordered; current text may contain outcome announcements (excluded semantically). Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote a specific factual claim from the original post and refute that same claim?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Output 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (verbatim or clearly marked near-verbatim excerpt) a specific factual claim stated in the OP text (title and argument) and (b) argues that this same claim is false, inaccurate or unsupported, within that same comment. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy the conjunction. Quoting opinions/values rather than factual claims, quoting without refuting, or refuting without quoting gives no credit. Quotation marks alone do not prove the text comes from the OP; check against the OP title/argument. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence. Output 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_factual_claim = 1 have a higher rate of view change than rows with 0.
decomposed.note: Presence (any comment) is assumed since no quantity was specified. OLS on binary delta gives a linear probability difference in rates; association only. OC_comments and the OP text may contain outcome announcements, and timing of comments relative to the outcome is unknown; these are excluded by the semantic spec as evidence. Factual vs. opinion claims is a judgment call.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.

features.name: validates_dignity_before_correcting
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the OP's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g., praising their effort, respecting their feelings/intent as a person) and (b) afterwards in that same comment introduces corrective logic (disagreement, counterpoint, or correction of reasoning). Validation must come before the corrective logic within the comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Generic politeness without reference to the OP's dignity/effort does not count. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 for a valid empty list or when no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: There is no difference in view-change rate between discussions with validates_dignity_before_correcting = 1 and those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with validates_dignity_before_correcting = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: The comparison group is "purely logical refutations", i.e. discussions with corrective logic but no dignity/effort validation. The feature's 0 group also includes discussions with no refutation at all and discussions where validation occurs without correction. The claimed comparison therefore cannot be measured exactly, and a not-A coefficient would not be the named contrast. Because no pure-logic-refutation measurement is defined, term is null. Reported associations only. conversation is not used. OC_comments may contain outcome-related text, and its timing relative to the outcome is unknown.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.

features.name: oc_has_concrete_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment provide a concrete real-world example as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Output 1 if at least one comment offers a specific, concrete real-world example (a real event, case, person, organization, personal experience, or data instance) as support for its counter-argument, in the commenter's own assertion or as an external source cited as support. Hypothetical/invented scenarios, generic abstract claims, and quotations of the OP or others that are merely rebutted do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements or reports of the outcome as evidence. Output 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if missing or malformed.

features.name: oc_primarily_abstract_reasoning
features.definition: Do the counter-argument comments rely primarily on abstract reasoning rather than concrete real-world examples?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP).
